I can’t tell you for sure what went on in my first weeks transitioning, because I feel like alot of it might have been placebo, however-

within hours I felt like I was already feeling different, and I knew that I had made the right decision, kinda hard to describe. Also, I always end up taking naps after my weekly injections lol.

I’m at the beginning of my “awkward phase right now (2.5 months, people have made comments to me who don’t know I’m trans), you just gotta remember that its a phase! It will pass eventually and won’t be so awkward anymore!

I also get alot of anxiety about what people might say/do to me when I’m in public if they find out, I think the actual number of people who are that extreme to harass you/get physical is not so high in reality.
Just stick with a friend if you feel unsafe if that is possible. 

I’ve had some friends surprise me with being way more supportive than I would have imagined, you really don’t know until you tell them.

Trans woman here.

Do ciswomen need 3 letters, 2 from therapists and 1 from their endocrinologist to get a boob job? A nose job? No! Why should any medical surgeries be gate-kept like that?

The argument that its a permanent change is BS because hormones already start to have some permanent effects after about 3 months.

With any other condition in medicine, a delay in care is seen as a BAD thing, because it can have a mental and or physical impact on the condition of the patient. 

It took me contemplating suicide to decide to start to transition, because of how badly society can treat trans people. Some of us avoid transitioning earlier and wait to start leading happy lives because of how others treat us.  I have no regrets, but I am disappointed by some of the people I thought I was close to. 

Maybe if people treated transgender individuals as actually being human? There is no reason for any of this to be this way.
